style_when: the article is a purely conceptual synthesis or policy dilemma where no physical facility, machine, or supply chain exists, and an elegant abstract paper silhouette states the idea. Never reach for paper collage when the story describes physical manufacturing, freight, energy, hardware, or heavy infrastructure — use cinematic still or telephoto industry instead
prompt: Split-screen editorial cut-paper collage on a control room desk. Left half: a lowered red-and-white barrier gate arm blocks a stack of graphite server modules cut from matte paper with halftone newsprint texture. Right half: a circular bone-white meter gauge with a safety-yellow needle points across a rust-red backing. Hand-torn rag paper with visible fiber, physical cast shadows under each layer, one raking light from the left, muted palette of graphite, safety yellow, bone white, generous negative space, no legible print.
rationale: Paper collage suits this conceptual policy dilemma: no physical facility or machine is the subject, so cut-paper silhouettes can state the gate-versus-meter contrast with editorial clarity and material presence. The split-screen diptych enforces the two-scenario duality required by the hard rules.
subject: a lowered approval gate arm blocking a stack of server modules contrasted with a unit-cost meter dial
core_thesis: AI spend moved from the pauseable fifth to the cost-of-revenue four-fifths, so the protective control is a unit-cost meter, not an approval gate.
core_conflict: Approval gates cut 20% of initiatives while unit-cost funding loses only 7%, because gates only reach the small pauseable development budget.
composition: split-screen diptych with left-right scenario contrast
